items.item: The grid header names the week with its date range (such as "Week 45 · 2–8 Nov 2026"), every day column shows the weekday and date, and controls move to the previous, next and current week
items.evidence: h2#week-range shows fmtRange(ui.weekStart) e.g. "02–08 thg 11, 2026"; each th in #day-header-row shows WEEKDAY_SHORT (T2..CN) plus day.getDate(); #btn-prev/#btn-next/#btn-today call addDays(±7)/reset to BASE_WEEK_START and re-render. No explicit 'Week N' number is shown, only the date range.

items.item: Each shift shows its start and end time in one consistent 24-hour format and the role or station (such as "07:00–15:00 · Cashier"), and a shift that ends after midnight is marked as ending the next day
items.evidence: cellContent() renders shift buttons as `${t.label}${entry.start}–${entry.end}` e.g. "Ca tối / 22:00–06:00" — consistent 24h time, but shows the shift-type label (Ca sáng/chiều/tối), not the employee's role/station (role only appears once per row under the name). The overnight 'Ca tối' shift (22:00–06:00) is rendered identically to same-day shifts with no '+1 day' / next-day marker anywhere in cellContent() or SHIFT_TYPES.

items.item: Each staff row shows the week's scheduled hours against contracted hours (such as "36 / 40 h"), the scheduled figure equals that person's shifts less unpaid breaks, and anyone over or under contract is flagged in words
items.evidence: Row's last cell is `weeklyHours(emp.id, days, weekData)` rendering a bare number (e.g. '48', '56', '32') via tnum span under header 'Tổng giờ'. EMPLOYEES objects (script line ~227) have no contracted-hours field, no '/40h' comparison, and no over/under-contract flag text anywhere.

items.item: A footer row shows, for each day, the staff count or hours scheduled against the required cover, and days below the requirement are marked in text (such as "Short 1")
items.evidence: renderCoverageRow() builds tfoot#coverage-row cells as `${scheduled}/${required}` plus `Thiếu ${required-scheduled}` when scheduled

items.item: The sample data contains at least one rule conflict, such as overlapping shifts for one person or less than 11 hours' rest between a closing and the next opening shift, shown on the affected cell with a written reason
items.evidence: No conflict-detection code exists anywhere in the script (no function compares rest gaps or overlaps). E.g. Lê Hoàng Cường has 'Ca tối 22:00–06:00' Wed then 'Ca sáng 06:00–14:00' Thu with 0h rest, but no cell is flagged, styled differently, or given a written reason for this.

items.item: Approved leave, days off and public holidays appear as labelled cells (such as "Annual leave", "Day off") that look different from an empty, unscheduled cell
items.evidence: 'Nghỉ' (Day off, bg-slate-50) and 'Nghỉ phép' (Annual leave, bg-slate-100 border-slate-300) are distinct from the empty '+' button (border-dashed text-slate-400) — but there is no public-holiday entry kind anywhere in entry.kind handling ('shift'|'off'|'leave'|'leave-pending'|'leave-continuation' only), so public holidays are not represented at all.

items.item: The week's status (Draft or Published) is shown, and publishing goes through a confirmation that names the week and the number of unresolved conflicts or warnings
items.evidence: #status-badge shows 'Dự thảo'/'Đã công bố'/'Có thay đổi mới' (Draft/Published/Changed) via renderHeaderStatus(). Clicking #btn-publish opens openConfirm() with title `Công bố lịch tuần ${fmtRange(...)}?` which names the week, but the body text is a static sentence about notifying staff — it never mentions a count of unresolved conflicts or warnings (consistent with no conflict detection existing).

items.item: The grid is a <table> with staff names as row headers and days as column headers, and each shift or empty cell is keyboard-reachable with an accessible name that includes the person and the date (such as "Add shift, Lan Pham, Tue 3 Nov")
items.evidence: <table class="w-full border-collapse"> with <th scope="row"> per employee name and <th scope="col"> per day; every cell button has aria-label built from `${emp.name}` + `${dayFull}` (e.g. 'Nguyễn Văn An, Ca sáng, 06:00–14:00, Thứ Hai, 02/11/2026' or 'Thêm ca cho X, <date>' for empty cells); roving tabindex + arrow-key navigation implemented in the #roster-rows keydown listener.

items.item: A week with no shifts yet shows a message with a way to start (such as "Copy last week"), and a loading state and a load error with a retry button exist
items.evidence: Loading state (data-state="loading", aria-busy, #skeleton) and error state (data-state="error", role="alert", #retry button) both exist and are wired (setTimeout(render,300), ?state=error). However the only 'empty' state (data-state="empty") is for a filtered-out employee list ('Không có nhân viên nào khớp' / Clear filters) — there is no scenario or UI for a week that genuinely has zero shifts, and no 'copy last week' or similar starter action exists anywhere in the script.

notes: Data generator (buildWeek/rand01) produces a fully-staffed week by construction, so several implemented-but-conditional features (coverage shortfall text, overnight-shift handling, conflict flags) either never trigger or were never built. No stylistic 'AI slop' tells were observed: no greeting header, no KPI icon tiles, no gradients/glass, no emoji icons, no uppercase tracked labels, standard 4-6px radii, muted slate sidebar with blue (not indigo) primary accent, hover states are subtle background-only. Primary gaps are functional: no contracted-hours comparison, no public holidays, no conflict/rest-rule detection, and no 'copy last week' / true empty-week flow.
